summary: Native Integration - Cvent (Event Management) — Phase 1: Inbound

ai.s: Adds a native inbound Cvent integration to the Integration Hub, syncing attendees and exhibitors into ExpoPlatform with delta polling and a custom-questions import helper.
ai.pr: Clients running events in Cvent had no native way to bring Cvent attendees and exhibitors into ExpoPlatform, so data had to be moved by other means.
ai.wy: Integration Hub expansion: native connectors to major event platforms make ExpoPlatform easier to adopt alongside existing client tooling.
ai.oc: A polled OAuth2 Cvent → EP sync on the AutoUpdate engine is specified, matched on External ID, with a helper to pre-fill registration sections from Cvent question definitions; push-back is Phase 2.

summary: Native Integration - Eventbrite — Phase 1: Inbound

ai.s: Adds a native inbound Eventbrite integration to the Integration Hub, importing Eventbrite attendees as visitors with delta sync.
ai.pr: Organisers selling tickets through Eventbrite had no native connector to bring those attendees into ExpoPlatform.
ai.wy: Integration Hub expansion to reduce manual data transfer for clients using Eventbrite.
ai.oc: A polled Eventbrite → EP visitor sync is specified, using a private OAuth2 bearer token, changed_since delta filtering and External ID matching; exhibitors are out of scope as Eventbrite has none.

summary: Introduce mandatory field mapping in data import

ai.s: Data import now blocks confirmation until each block's mandatory system fields are mapped, flagging the missing fields in the mapping popup.
ai.pr: Admins could confirm an import without mapping essential fields such as participant email or product owner, producing incomplete or broken records.
ai.wy: Data quality: prevent bad imports at the point of mapping rather than cleaning up afterwards.
ai.oc: Per-block mandatory fields (e.g. First Name, Last Name, Email for participants) are defined; Confirm stays disabled and unmapped fields are named until all are mapped.

summary: Implement Microsoft Clarity in Admin Panel

ai.s: Adds Microsoft Clarity session recordings and heatmaps to the Admin Panel so Product can see how organiser clients actually use key workflows.
ai.pr: Product had no behavioural evidence of how organisers use the Admin Panel and relied on anecdotal support tickets to find friction.
ai.wy: A low-compliance-overhead first phase of EP-51003 analytics, shipped ahead of the slower GA4 legal review.
ai.oc: Clarity is to be deployed with masking on, separate staging and production projects and consent handling, gated on Legal updating the sub-processor list.

summary: Native Integration - Salesforce (CRM) — Phase 1: Inbound

ai.s: Adds a native inbound Salesforce integration to the Integration Hub, syncing Contacts or Leads as visitors and Accounts as exhibitors.
ai.pr: Clients holding exhibitor and visitor data in Salesforce had no native connector to import it into ExpoPlatform.
ai.wy: Integration Hub expansion: CRM connectors reduce manual data handling and support client adoption.
ai.oc: A polled Salesforce → EP sync via SOQL on SystemModStamp is specified, with Connected App OAuth, External ID matching and daily API-limit awareness; push-back is Phase 2.

summary: Native Integration - Cvent (Event Management) — Phase 2: Push-Back

ai.s: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Cvent integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates, including profile pictures and logos, back to Cvent.
ai.pr: The Phase 1 Cvent integration was inbound only, so changes made in ExpoPlatform never reached the client's Cvent records.
ai.wy: Two-way sync keeps client systems of record current without manual re-entry.
ai.oc: Independently toggleable visitor, exhibitor and image push-back subscriptions are specified, reusing Phase 1 auth and ID mapping, with image-loop prevention flagged as a risk.

summary: Native Integration - HubSpot (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back

ai.s: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the HubSpot integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to HubSpot Contacts and Companies.
ai.pr: The Phase 1 HubSpot integration was inbound only, so updates made in ExpoPlatform did not flow back to the client's CRM.
ai.wy: Two-way CRM sync keeps client data consistent across systems.
ai.oc: Toggleable push-back subscriptions with a dedicated outbound field mapping are specified, needing extra write scopes; image push-back is not possible on HubSpot.

summary: Native Integration - Salesforce (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back

ai.s: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Salesforce integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to Salesforce Contacts, Leads and Accounts.
ai.pr: The Phase 1 Salesforce integration was inbound only, so ExpoPlatform-side changes did not reach the client's Salesforce records.
ai.wy: Two-way CRM sync for clients whose system of record is Salesforce.
ai.oc: Toggleable push-back with its own outbound mapping is specified, sharing Phase 1 credentials and the daily API quota; image push-back is not applicable.

summary: Unify favouriting into FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers

ai.s: Consolidates all favouriting into one FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers instead of controller switch statements.
ai.pr: Favourite flows branched by object type in controller switches, and FavouriteService only handled the opted-out private path while public writes stayed in controllers and models.
ai.wy: Follow-up from the EP-53978 / PR #4431 review to reduce duplication and keep new favouriting logic in one place.
ai.oc: A single service with visitor, exhibitor, product, brand and session handlers is planned, with public writes migrating gradually and reads optionally consolidated.

summary: Bulk connection delete is not private-favourite-aware

ai.s: Bulk connection delete now also removes opted-out users' private favourites, so they can bulk-remove what they bulk-added.
ai.pr: Bulk add correctly stored opted-out users' favourites privately, but bulk delete only touched account_connections and returned not_found for those private rows.
ai.wy: Found in QA scope inventory of the EP-53978 private favourites work; the asymmetry broke the mobile bulk-remove flow.
ai.oc: Bulk delete is aligned with single-disconnect behaviour and removes the owner's private favourite rows; the fix is in testing.

summary: N+1 queries in V3 Sponsors list — exhibitor logo gate resolves per-sponsor at serialization

ai.s: Removes an N+1 query pattern in the V3 Sponsors list, where each sponsor's exhibitor logo setting was resolved separately at serialisation.
ai.pr: SponsorResource::toArray() called getGatedImageUrl() per sponsor, lazily loading the linked exhibitor's effective settings with fresh database reads each time.
ai.wy: Performance regression introduced by EP-47975's exhibitor logo gating on the sponsor chain.
ai.oc: Logo gating is to be resolved once per page rather than per sponsor, keeping the same image output.

summary: Enforce view-only / event scope for admin permissions (deny-by-default in AccessControl)

ai.s: Makes admin permissions deny-by-default so an admin set to view-only or no access on one event no longer gets full access on every other event.
ai.pr: AccessControl fell back to a permissive global default row for any event without an explicit permission row, so per-event restrictions did not hold across events.
ai.wy: Security finding split out of the EP-55010 admin lockout investigation; restricted admins could act on events they should not.
ai.oc: The fix to fetchAccessZone is scoped with explicit caution, as a naive deny-by-default could lock out many production admins across tenants.

summary: [BE] Global rate-limit for Utils::sendException with repeat counting

ai.s: Adds a global rate limit with repeat counting to exception notifications, so an outage no longer floods the alert channel with identical messages.
ai.pr: Utils::sendException() sent a notification on every call, so a failing dependency under traffic drowned other alerts in duplicates.
ai.wy: Generalises the local AI-search rate limit from EP-47675 to the whole platform and removes that workaround.
ai.oc: A per-call-site signature with memcached marker and counter suppresses repeats for 300s, reports the repeat count next time and fails open if the cache is down.

summary: [TechDept] [EP:dev] N+1 in participant export getParticipantData — per-event 'SELECT title' query per account (N×M events queries)

ai.s: Removes an N+1 in participant export, where a separate event-title query ran for every account and every event it was active in.
ai.pr: ExportTask::getParticipantData() issued an uncached SELECT title per account per active event, giving N×M+N queries and refetching the same titles.
ai.wy: Performance defect found in audit (moderate severity) on the export hot loop.
ai.oc: Event titles are to be loaded once and reused across the export, including the moderator all-events branch, with unchanged output.

summary: reduce dev-mode compilation graph: lazy-load heavy layout subtrees and enable webpack lazyCompilation

ai.s: Cuts portal-ui dev-mode page compile times by lazy-loading heavy layout subtrees and enabling webpack lazyCompilation.
ai.pr: Each dev page transition compiled 11.5k–16k modules and took 20–35s, because the shared layout statically pulled in the form builder, draft-js and the messenger.
ai.wy: Developer productivity: slow dev compiles waste engineering time on every page change.
ai.oc: Measured with lazyCompilation: profile 35s to 15.7s, news 20s to 10.6s, groups 21.5s to 3.7s, with per-page graphs down to 9.9k–12.3k modules.

summary: Add relevant logs to data import

ai.s: Each data import produces a result log, with a summary in Log Info and a downloadable per-row file showing what was created, updated or skipped and why.
ai.pr: Admins could not confirm what an import created or updated, or see which rows were skipped and for what reason.
ai.wy: Import transparency, so admins can trust and fix imports, especially where duplicates arise from fake email generation settings.
ai.oc: A summary with counts, status and fake-email state is logged, plus the uploaded file echoed back with Row, Action and Reason columns for re-upload.

summary: File size upload issue on data import

ai.s: Lets admins import one data file of any size and get one trustworthy result, instead of splitting large files by hand.
ai.pr: Large imports could not be processed in one pass, and manual splitting caused broken records, duplicate accounts across files and fragmented result logs.
ai.wy: Data integrity during bulk onboarding ahead of events, when errors matter most.
ai.oc: Required behaviours are set: one upload is one job and re-running after an interruption never duplicates data; the processing design is left to the team.

summary: [BE-NonTM]Translation: please apply the missing system translations.

ai.s: Adds missing and corrected EN/DE notification translations for Frankfurter Buchmesse and DLG PotatoEurope exhibitors on live events.
ai.pr: Exhibitor notifications on live FBM and DLG events had missing German translations and wrong English wording, which could not be fixed in Translation Manager.
ai.wy: Urgent client need: the events were live and exhibitors were already using the platform.
ai.oc: Approval and time-change notification strings are to be added and corrected in EN and DE.

summary: Move account creation earlier in Registration flow (prerequisite for cart approach) - ON HOLD

epic.summary: On Hold Registration Stories and Post Registration work

ai.s: Creates the registrant's account before payment starts rather than after submission, as a prerequisite for the cart payment approach (on hold).
ai.pr: The account was created by a post-commit listener after the registration transaction, so no account_id existed when payment began.
ai.wy: Blocks the cart/basket payment approach in EP-55566, which needs a reserved account before payment.
ai.oc: Draft criteria move account creation ahead of payment, update ordering tests and audit dependent code; the story is on hold.

summary: Handle VAT charged when VAT-number check service is unavailable at checkout - ON HOLD

epic.summary: On Hold Registration Stories and Post Registration work

ai.s: Defines how checkout should handle VAT when the VAT-number check service is down, instead of silently overcharging exempt business customers (on hold).
ai.pr: When the VAT-number check was unavailable, VAT was charged even to reverse-charge B2B customers, and correction relied on someone noticing and refunding manually.
ai.wy: Invoice correctness and tax compliance; overcharged customers need formal invoice corrections.
ai.oc: Options to block checkout, charge and auto-correct with a refund and credit note, or retry are set out for a product and engineering decision; on hold.
